business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Importation of Deep-Frozen Meat Carcasses and Pelagic Fish

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: civil law for private and commercial matters under the Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), including partnership law and the societe en commandite regime; common law in federal public law, criminal law, and federal regulatory fields; dual federal-provincial AML/CFT enforcement architecture.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), in force 1 July 2020
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), in provisional application since 21 September 2017
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force for Canada 30 December 2018
Canada-China Income Tax Agreement (1986) DTA, in force and applicable to Quebec as an intergovernmental tax agreement
Investment Canada Act (RSC 1985, c 28 (1st Supp.)) - statutory foreign investment review regime governing non-Canadian control of Canadian businesses

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 and companion FINTRAC regulations (PCMLTFR, SOR/2002-184); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part II.1 (terrorist financing); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Regulations Implementing the United Nations Resolutions on the Suppression of Terrorism; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 (arts 2.4, 9-13, 25.1-25.10) and Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r 1, imposing mandatory ultimate beneficiary (UBO) declaration with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec; Investment Canada Act for foreign investor notification and net-benefit review thresholds; Quebec Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, for mandatory French-language registration and translation of corporate filings.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access: UBO declarations are filed electronically with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec and are accessible only to authorized bodies (corporate registry, provincial and federal tax authorities, police, financial intelligence units, and AML reporting entities acting under legal mandate); not publicly searchable.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of existence / good standing of the foreign corporate general partner (preuve d'existence de la personne morale constituee hors Quebec)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or notary public in the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Hague Convention) issued by the competent authority of the issuing state; if the issuing state is not a Hague member, consular legalization at the competent Canadian diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney designating the local representative or registration agent with authority to sign the declaration of registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of the ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified ownership-chain extract identifying each ultimate beneficial owner of each tier, including names, nationalities, identification numbers, and control percentages
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent, corporate registry, or auditing firm in the origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declaration and PEP status questionnaire executed by each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-clearance screening of all UBOs, general partners, directors, and authorized representatives against (i) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (ii) Canadian sanctions regulations enacted under SEMA and the United Nations Act (including those targeting Russia, Belarus, Iran, North Korea, Venezuela, Syria, Myanmar, and other designated persons and sectors); (iii) FINTRAC published lists and OFAC SDN list as a best-practice overlay; (iv) domestic Canadian and Quebec politically exposed persons registers. Foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs in high public office, and heads of international organizations must be identified under PCMLTFA s 11(1), triggering enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Suspicious transaction reporting under PCMLTFA ss 7-7.1 applies without threshold minimums.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - online name clearance, reservation, and corporate registration portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the sole official language under the Charter of the French Language. The societe en commandite must have a French-language name; a non-French name or a transliteration of a non-Latin script may be used only in addition to and combined with a French version. All REQ filings, including the declaration of registration and UBO schedule, must be completed in French using official government forms; ancillary documents in other languages require certified translation into French by a certified Quebec translator (OATIAQ member) before filing.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Financial-sector terms ('Banque', 'Fiduciaire', 'Caisse', 'Assurance', 'Finance') requiring authorization from the Autorite des marches financiers (AMF) or OSFI
Government or Crown terms ('Societe de la Couronne', 'Commission', 'Office', 'Ministere', 'Municipalite', 'Revenu')
Terms contrary to public order, morality, or decency, and names likely to mislead as to the nature, activity, or geographic scope of the business
Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name in the REQ enterprise register or in another Canadian provincial registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal, REQ issues a written decision stating the statutory grounds. The applicant may (i) file a corrected name reservation request online with a revised French name and any ministerial authorization letters for sensitive tokens, or (ii) appeal the refusal to the Tribunal administratif du Quebec (TAQ) within 30 days of notification under art 75 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, attaching the REQ refusal letter, the original reservation receipt, and legal arguments on registrability. A name reservation may be extended once by filing a renewal request with the prescribed fee before expiry if the declaration of registration has not yet been completed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical establishment in Quebec is mandatory for the societe en commandite under arts 9-13 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. The registered office may be the address of the general partner or a licensed registered-agent office in Montreal; a virtual-office/reception-services address is acceptable for the registration stage and general administrative correspondence, provided it is a real, accessible physical address at which legal documents can be produced and process served. A post-office box is prohibited. For cold-chain meat and seafood importation, a virtual office cannot substitute for the operating establishment (cold storage, customs-bonded warehouse or terminal receiving facility) that CFIA and MAPAQ will require once the import licence and Safe Food for Canadians Act registration are sought in later stages.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Registration-stage inspection risk by REQ is low: approximately 5-10% of newly registered partnerships are randomly selected for documentary or on-site compliance audits in a given year. However, statistical risk rises sharply post-licensing: over 80% of new federally licensed food importers receive an unannounced CFIA and/or MAPAQ physical inspection within the first 12 months of operation, including cold-chain facility, HACCP plan, import documentation, and product traceability reviews. REQ inspectors, under arts 54-62 of P-44.1, may enter premises, audit records, and seize documents without prior notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c. CCQ), arts. 2186 and 2237-2263 (Limited Partnership — société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-45), ss. 2, 11-26, 83 (registration, firm name, and register authority); Taxation Act (CQLR c. I-3) for provincial tax registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), administered under the Inspectorate General of Financial Institutions (IGIF), Ministère des Finances du Québec; principal office at 2050 rue de Bleury, Montréal, Québec; online service at registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) — the constitutive public filing for a limited partnership under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; upon deposit with the REQ, the société en commandite attains juridical personality and is issued a Québec Enterprise Number (NEQ).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Québec limited partnership; partners freely determine contributions in the written partnership agreement, provided each limited partner's contribution is in money or property, not services (art. 2255 C.c.Q.). No escrow account is mandated by law; however, funds for the trade-finance rails (revolving letters of credit, SWIFT TT) should be held in a Schedule I Canadian bank account in the partnership's name, and a Canadian custodian bank account is standard practice to evidence the capital subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: INITIAL RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF GENERAL PARTNER INC. — RESOLVED: (1) THAT the Corporation, as sole general partner, approves the subscription of the partnership units in Mandataire LP II (the 'Partnership') to be constituted under Articles 2237-2263 C.c.Q.; (2) THAT the Corporation adopts the limited partnership agreement and declares the registered office of the Partnership at [address in Province of Quebec]; (3) THAT the President and the Secretary are authorized to execute and file the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and to open the Partnership's bank account; (4) THAT the President and Secretary are appointed as managing partner officers, with general authority to enter into trade finance, import license, and customs broker agreements. CARRIED.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Firm Name Search and Name Reservation with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online name search and reservation module (registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca); collaboration with the Centre de renseignements et de services for name acceptability.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a Quebec limited partnership name search in the REQ database, ensuring the firm name contains the mandatory designation 'société en commandite' or 's.e.c.' and does not include the name of any limited partner (art. 2254 C.c.Q.). Submit an Application for Name Reservation via the REQ portal, rank three proposed names, state the proposed objects (NAICS 424420, wholesale importation of deep-frozen meat carcasses and pelagic fish), and pay the prescribed reservation fee. The REQ then issues a Name Reservation Certificate valid for 90 days, allowing exclusive use of the reserved name for the formation filings.
required_dossiers: Three ranked proposed firm names ending in 's.e.c.' or 'société en commandite'
Copy of the general partner's incorporation certificate or NEQ confirmation if the general partner is already registered
Brief objective declaration identifying wholesale frozen beef and seafood importation (ISIC 4632 / NAICS 424420)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised name application adding a distinctive element, or request an individual name analysis by the REQ within the statutory review period; a formal refusal may be contested by way of administrative review before the Inspector General of Financial Institutions and thereafter by judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement (Convention de Société en Commandite)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaries and legal counsel in Quebec; private deed sufficient unless an immovable asset is contributed, in which case an authentic notarial act is required under art. 2268 C.c.Q.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a written limited partnership agreement between the general partner and the initial limited partners. The agreement must define capital contributions, profit and loss allocation ratios, the passive role of limited partners, transfer restrictions, dissolution events, and the general partner's exclusive power of administration. If any contribution consists of immovable property, the agreement must be passed before a notary and published; if contributions are movable or cash, a private deed executed by all partners suffices. The agreement must be fully signed before the Declaration of Registration is deposited with the REQ.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement (Convention de société en commandite / s.e.c.) executed by all partners
Identity and address evidence of each general and limited partner
Capital contribution schedule and confirmation of the fund transfer routing for the initial contribution
Passive-investor confirmation from each limited partner confirming non-participation in management (preservation of limited liability)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a clause would expose limited partners to unlimited liability (e.g., participation in management or absence of the 's.e.c.' suffix), rectify the agreement and re-execute before filing; where a notarial deed is required and the parties executed privately, re-execute as an authentic act and reinstate the filing timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of the Declaration of Registration and Issuance of the Québec Enterprise Number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Registraire Express online e-filing system; paper filing counter at 2050 rue de Bleury, Montréal, Québec.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and transmit the Déclaration d'immatriculation for the limited partnership via Registraire Express. Insert the reserved firm name, the legal form 'société en commandite (s.e.c.)', the registered office address in Quebec, the declaration of objects (wholesale importation and distribution of deep-frozen beef carcasses and pelagic fish products), the general partner's name and NEQ, and the date of execution of the partnership agreement. Pay the prescribed e-filing registration fee (CAD 46.38). Upon deposit, the Limited Partnership becomes a juridical person, is assigned its NEQ, and receives an attestation d'immatriculation with a full copy of the register entry; the attestation is the legal basis for all subsequent federal, provincial, and municipal licensing.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Certificate (Certificat de réservation de nom)
Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation) — Form AR-001 or the Registraire Express online equivalent
Proof of the partnership's registered office address in Quebec (lease, sub-lease, or occupancy authorization)
Power of attorney of the filing representative if submission is made by a third-party agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a notice of deficiency or refuses the declaration, cure the deficiencies (e.g., invalid registered office address, missing general partner identification, non-conforming firm name) and resubmit the amended declaration within the delay prescribed in the notice; an administrative review may be filed with the REQ, followed by judicial recourse before the Superior Court of Quebec under the Code of Civil Procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registration — Business Number, GST/HST, QST and Import/Export (Customs) Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration On-Line service and Business Window (1-800-959-5525); Revenu Québec — Cl@ss Affaires portal for QST and employer accounts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership's Business Number with the CRA immediately upon issuance of the NEQ. Create the GST/HST program account (RT0001), required when annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 or voluntarily for input tax credit recovery; the Import/Export (Customs) program account (RM0001) must be opened with the CBSA importer number for the first customs entry. Register the QST account (NR0001 and/or NR0002) with Revenu Québec linking the NEQ, and confirm the partnership's pass-through reporting through the federal T5013 Information Return and the Quebec TP-600 partnership return. Arrange any non-resident partner withholding accounts as applicable.
required_dossiers: REQ attestation d'immatriculation showing the partnership's NEQ
General partner's incorporation or registration identification documents
Estimated annual taxable sales for GST/HST and QST purposes (threshold CAD 30,000)
Details of non-resident limited partners to assess withholding and reporting obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects an account application for an identity or address mismatch, correct the NEQ data with REQ and re-apply online; if Revenu Québec issues a query, file the reconciliation schedule electronically and, where an account was wrongly denied, escalate through the tax services office business window or file a notice of objection within the prescribed time.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CFIA Safe Food for Canadians Act Import Licence, Preventive Control Plan and Cold-Chain Border Program
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) — Safe Food for Canadians Branch (My CFIA portal); Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for import entry and eManifest; Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ) for provincial food sector oversight.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online through the My CFIA portal for a Safe Food for Canadians Act (SFCA) Import Licence in the 'Importing Food' class covering the sub-categories of frozen beef and pelagic fish products. Prepare and submit the Preventive Control Plan (PCP) describing the receiving, cold storage, and distribution controls, including confirmation of storage at -18 degrees Celsius and the foreign supplier equivalency documentation. Upon license issuance, connect the licence to the CBSA customs entry profile and the eManifest process, and retain a licensed customs broker for the first consignments. Register the operational cold-storage address with MAPAQ under the provincial food safety surveillance framework.
required_dossiers: Safe Food for Canadians Act Import Licence application filed electronically via My CFIA
Preventive Control Plan covering receiving, frozen storage, thawing controls, and shipping of frozen beef and pelagic fish
Official health or export certificates from the country of origin for the initial qualified consignments
Cold-chain protocol confirming continuous storage at -18 degrees Celsius and schedule of licensed third-party cold storage warehouses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CFIA issues a deficiency letter or an administrative monetary penalty, respond within 30 days with a corrective action plan and third-party HACCP validation; if the licence is refused for PCP inadequacy, amend the PCP, obtain independent audit verification, and re-submit; CFIA enforcement actions may be appealed under the Safe Food for Canadians Regulations review mechanism and thereafter to the Federal Court if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Industrial Establishment Permit, Fire and Structural Clearance, and Environmental Conformity Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ville de Montréal or the applicable local municipality — Service de l'urbanisme et permis d'exploitation; local Service de sécurité incendie; Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP); Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File for the municipal commercial/industrial establishment permit (permis d'exploitation) for the cold-chain warehouse, submitting the zoning certificate, architectural and refrigeration drawings, and fire safety plans. Obtain the fire safety certification from the local fire service, including sprinkler acceptance and cold-room egress approvals, and a structural load certificate for pallet racking and mezzanine storage. Submit the MELCCFP refrigerant registration declaration for the refrigeration systems (HFC/F-gas inventory and leakage monitoring), and confirm the municipal sewer discharge conformity for any thawing or wash bay. A full environmental impact assessment is generally not required for a wholesale cold-storage warehouse of this classification.
required_dossiers: Commercial/industrial establishment permit application to the local municipality
Engineer-certified structural and refrigeration drawings for the cold storage facility
Fire safety certificate and sprinkler system certification from the local fire service
MELCCFP refrigerant registration declaration including HFC inventory and annual leakage inspection commitment
Municipal sewer discharge conformity declaration for wash bays and thawing areas
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal permit is refused or delayed, seek a hearing before the municipal building authority or adjustment committee and supplement the drawings; if MELCCFP reclassifies the facility as requiring a ministerial authorization due to larger ammonia volumes, file a declaration of conformity or environmental impact assessment under the Loi sur la qualité de l'environnement and pause operations until authorization; CNESST stop-work orders are cured by implementing the prescribed corrective preventive measures and obtaining re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) — Safe Food for Canadians Branch, with provincial co-supervision by the Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ) and municipal industrial permitting through the local municipality (e.g., Ville de Montréal).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Safe Food for Canadians Act Import Licence (Importation of Meat and Fish Products) issued under the Safe Food for Canadians Regulations, together with the municipal industrial establishment permit (permis d'exploitation d'un établissement commercial ou industriel) for the cold storage warehouse.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Gouvernement du Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 'C' — Declaration of conformity / attestation of exemption (avis d'absence d'obligation de procéder à une évaluation environnementale): a wholesale cold-chain import warehouse storing frozen beef and pelagic fish products is typically exempt from a full environmental impact assessment; a full EIA or ministerial authorization is triggered only where large ammonia-based refrigeration systems or substantial fish-processing effluent discharges are present.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L, COD ≤ 700 mg/L, total suspended solids ≤ 450 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.0, fats, oils and grease ≤ 15 mg/L per municipal sewer bylaws (Montreal Agglomeration wastewater regulation); Refrigerants: compliance with the Canadian Ozone-depleting Substances and Halocarbon Alternatives Regulations and the Quebec Clean Air Regulation, including the Kigali Amendment HFC phase-down, annual leak testing and record-keeping; Waste handling: cold-chain packaging and offal waste must be managed under the Quebec Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of residual materials.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification under the Quebec Construction Code and the National Fire Code of Canada, issued by the local Service de sécurité incendie, including automatic sprinkler acceptance, cold-room emergency egress, and hazardous refrigerant detection; Structural load inspection by a licensed engineer for the pallet racking system and freezer mezzanine; Occupational health and safety clearance from CNESST under the Act respecting occupational health and safety, including cold-environment work protection plans; municipal certificate of occupancy (certificat d'occupation) for the warehouse unit.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec. In Quebec, Revenu Québec administers both the federal GST (under a single administration agreement) and the provincial QST. Corporate income tax filings for the LP are made to both CRA and Revenu Québec. Portal: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html and https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from CRA using Form RC1 or the Business Registration Online (BRO) service, including a GST/HST program account (RT) and possibly an import/export program account (RM). In parallel, register with Revenu Québec to obtain a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and a QST account (account identifier derived from the NEQ). Non-residents must appoint a Canadian representative and supply a domestic address for service. After registration, the LP receives separate BN/NEQ credentials and must file mandatory registrations with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec if carrying on commercial activity in Québec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not permit a full US-style check-the-box election. The limited partnership is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes; no election is available to treat it as a corporation. Relevant statutory elections include: (a) subsection 216(1) Income Tax Act election for non-resident partners to compute Canadian-source income tax on a net basis; (b) subsection 97(2) rollover election on transfers of capital property to the partnership; (c) GST/HST elections under section 156 of the Excise Tax Act (closely related persons) to treat certain supplies as made for nil consideration, where applicable. Hybrid mismatch rules (sections 18.4 and 18.5 ITA) may apply to deductible payments involving partnerships with differing tax characterizations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of annual worldwide taxable supplies for GST/HST and QST registration; non-residents importing goods into Canada may be required to register regardless of threshold to obtain input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping is currently implemented in Canada or Quebec. Electronic invoicing is permitted and legally equivalent to paper invoices if it contains required GST/HST/QST invoice information. CRA and Revenu Québec accept electronic records and filings via their portals; however, a comprehensive pan-Canadian e-invoicing mandate with API-based clearance is not yet in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods (including frozen beef and seafood) are zero-rated for GST/HST and QST under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act and corresponding Quebec legislation. The exporter must hold the goods continuously in Canada and export them by way of sale to a destination outside Canada within a reasonable period (normally 60 days). Commercial invoices, customs declarations, and written proof of exportation must be retained. Services supplied to a non-resident (including storage, logistics, and brokerage relating to export sales) qualify for zero-rating only where they are performed wholly or mainly outside Canada or are directly connected to the non-resident's export business.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may audit export invoices and customs records. If zero-rating is applied fraudulently or without proper documentation, penalties apply under the Excise Tax Act (sections 280.1, 285) and Quebec taxation laws. Gross negligence penalties may reach 25% of the tax claimed, and clawbacks of input tax credits (ITCs) can be made for four years (or longer for misrepresentation). Criminal prosecution can lead to fines up to CAD 200,000 and imprisonment up to 18 months. Participation in the Voluntary Disclosure Program may reduce penalties. Export documentation must be retained for at least six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential bank supervision by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); AML/ATF supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Canada has no separate foreign exchange control authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility. The Canadian dollar floats freely; there are no exchange controls, counterparty restrictions, or central bank approvals for capital injections, trade settlements, or profit remittances. Repatriation of profits is not FX-restricted. The only material statutory hurdles are federal and provincial income tax filing obligations, Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act on specified payments to non-residents (e.g. interest, rent, royalties, management fees), and the Investment Canada Act notification or review regime for foreign investments that acquire control of a Canadian business. For a Quebec limited partnership, current-account trade flows and capital-account injections can be settled freely in CAD, USD, or other foreign currency through a Schedule I bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender, conversion, or waiting-period rule for export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained in any freely convertible currency in domestic or foreign bank accounts. Administrative reporting obligations apply only for anti-money-laundering purposes: financial institutions must report electronic funds transfers and large-cash/transaction records of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC, and any person importing or exporting monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more must report to the Canada Border Services Agency. There is no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/USD multi-currency) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (CAD/USD) and Trade Settlement Account
Operational Account and Commercial Letter of Credit / Trade Account
Operational Commodity and Trade Finance Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for ancillary receivables/payables and foreign-currency disbursement, Low as the primary treasury or escrow rail. Canada has no EU-style EMI licence; offshore digital EMIs operating in Canada must register as money services businesses (MSB) with FINTRAC for foreign-exchange, remittance, and money-transfer activities, and may be subject to the future Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) regime. They may not accept deposits in Canada, as deposit-taking is reserved for chartered banks under the Bank Act. Offshore EMIs can only provide virtual currency accounts or pass-through settlement if they maintain a correspondent or virtual-IBAN arrangement with a Canadian Schedule I bank. Major Canadian banks often treat wires originating from an unregistered EMI as higher risk, and may reject or freeze funds if travel-rule information is incomplete.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not an absolute statutory rule under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, but in practice Canadian Schedule I banks mandate an in-person KYC interview for a non-resident-owned Quebec limited partnership. The general partner, a designated authorized signatory, or the principal beneficial owner is usually required to attend a branch meeting in Canada, especially where the LP has no Canadian directors or premises. Remote onboarding by video is available at certain banks for low-risk structures and simple ownership layers, but non-resident partners and regulated wholesale food importers normally trigger enhanced due diligence. A Quebec notarial or legalized copy of the partnership agreement is typically required, and certified true copies of passports and proof of address for all controlling persons must be presented.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of limited partnership beneficial ownership and absence of a corporate general partner with a substantive Canadian nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized or legalized partnership agreement, certificate of limited partnership from the Quebec enterprise registrar (Registraire des entreprises), an organizational chart identifying all general partners, limited partners holding 25% or more, and any indirect owners, plus certified copies of passports, government-issued ID, proof of residential address, tax residence certificates, and a source-of-wealth and source-of-funds narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners resident in high-risk or weakly regulated jurisdictions, or unrestricted general-power-of-attorney arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: For each non-resident owner: certified due diligence package, bank reference letters from their home-regulated bank, source of funds documentation such as audited financial statements, tax returns, payroll records, sale agreements or inheritance certificates, and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for the ownership structure. Any power of attorney must be limited, notarized, and accompanied by the underlying capacity and board authority documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frozen beef and pelagic seafood import profile raising sanctions, origin, customs, and food-safety red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete supply-chain evidence: CFIA import eligibility confirmation, Canadian Food Inspection Agency import permits where applicable, CBSA customs entry and B3 forms, bill of lading, air/sea waybill, packing lists, commercial invoices, HACCP and cold-chain temperature logs, supplier registration documents, health and veterinary certificates, country-of-origin certificates, and the underlying purchase contract or confirmed letter of credit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large volume of rapid incoming and outgoing cross-border wires inconsistent with the declared wholesale food trading business model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Forward treasury plan, buyer/supplier master list, transaction flow mapping between purchase orders, LC drawings, and invoice settlements; three-way matching of invoices, bills of lading, and LC documents; monthly aging reports from logistics providers; bank statements from the originator country; and a written description of the physical goods flow, storage facilities, and consignment freezing thresholds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from parent or foreign partners must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the remitting bank to the Canadian beneficiary bank. Canada does not use IBAN; the beneficiary must be identified using the Canadian financial institution number, branch transit number, and account number, together with the limited partnership legal name and account currency. Remittance information must state the purpose clearly, e.g. 'LP capital contribution'. The receiving Canadian bank will verify the sending bank's SWIFT/BIC, the originator and beneficiary legal entity names, and compliance with FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reporting above CAD 10,000. The funds may be converted to CAD or retained in USD under standing instructions. No Bank of Canada approval is required for the inflow. If the contribution confers 'control' of a Canadian business under the Investment Canada Act, a notification or review application may also be required, and all partnership capital accounts should be mirrored in the Quebec LP's records and tax filings.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For import settlement to foreign beef and seafood suppliers, preferred rails are SWIFT MT103 for open-account and advance payments, and SWIFT MT700/MT707 commercial letters of credit for deferred or documentary settlements, issued under UCP600. CAD-denominated domestic legs clear through Payments Canada Lynx; USD legs clear through CHIPS or FedWire via the Canadian bank's US correspondents. Typical documentary requirements under the LC include commercial invoice, full set of bills of lading made out to order, marine insurance certificate, packing list, certificate of origin, health/phytosanitary certificates, and cold-chain temperature records. For revolving trade flows, a Revolving LC facility is recommended, supplemented by SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for smaller open-account cargoes. All outbound disbursements must match an underlying import transaction and preserve the three-way documentary consistency required by AML/KYC reviews.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD FX forward contracts under ISDA or Canadian Bankers Association master agreements
CAD/USD cross-currency swaps (cross-currency interest rate swaps) for matched-funding of LC facilities
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market supplier currencies
Vanilla FX options and option collars for budget-rate protection
FX swaps to manage receivable-to-payable timing gaps

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual enterprise declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 calendar days after the registration anniversary date, or on the next business day if the deadline falls on a weekend or statutory holiday.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers administrative penalties and a default notice; persistent non-filing may result in administrative deregistration of the limited partnership from the REQ register, loss of name protection, and inability to validly carry on business in Quebec.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and partner allocation slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than five months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period; for a calendar-year fiscal period, due by March 31 of the following year unless extended by CRA.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs per-day penalties, minimum penalty amounts, and additional penalties for each incomplete or incorrect partner slip; continued default may expose the general partner to gross-negligence penalties and interest accrual.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec partnership information declaration (TP-600 / RL-31 information package) for the fiscal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within six months after the partnership's fiscal period-end; a nil return remains mandatory while the partnership is registered in Quebec.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers interest and late-filing penalties; material omissions can result in assessment by Revenu Québec and suspension of the partnership's provincial registration or tax accounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit applies to a non-reporting Quebec limited partnership under ordinary corporatelaw. A certified independent audit becomes contractually or regulatorily required where the partnership agreement calls for it, where a secured lender or issuing bank requires audited financial statements in support of a revolving LC facility, or where the partnership qualifies as a reporting issuer under Quebec securities legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian generally accepted accounting principles; private limited partnerships may prepare annual financial statements under ASPE or IFRS. IFRS is required for any partnership reporting to consolidated group financial statements or financial institutions under IFRS-based covenants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec's REQ does not require a separate annual UBO declaration for an ordinary limited partnership; the mandatory annual declaration must, however, reflect all changes in general and limited partners. A corporate general partner that is incorporated under Quebec or federal law must maintain its register of individuals with significant control and affirm or update it in its own annual filing. The LP must also maintain an internal beneficial-ownership and KYC/AML file for each limited partner, including confirming in writing each year that no unreported transfer of limited partnership interests has occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners and Capital Contributions
Register of Transfers and Assignments of Partnership Interests
Minute Book containing partnership resolutions, consents, and annual meeting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120–350 per year (CAD 160–470) for a Quebec registered office, service of process, and annual agent compliance handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500–14,000 for the first-year certified audit; USD 3,000–8,000 in subsequent years depending on partner count, transaction volume, and import financing requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (combined federal 15% + Quebec 11.5% for general corporations; note: LP is pass-through, partners taxed at their own rates)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction for CCPCs (not applicable to LP); manufacturing and processing profits deduction (not typical for importers); investment tax credits for qualified activities (e.g., scientific research, clean energy)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 (Federal Partnership Information Return) – CRA My Business Account
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., if year-end Dec 31, due May 31)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income from wholesale importation of frozen meat and seafood
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Canadian-source income; non-resident partners must receive allocation schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be reasonable and supported by documentation; non-resident partners cannot claim personal deductions
Allocate net income to each partner based on partnership agreement; non-resident partners taxed on Canadian-source business income if carrying on business in Canada

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide each non-resident partner with a T5013 slip; they must file Canadian tax return if income is taxable

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: $25 per day per partner, up to $2,500 per partner; additional penalty of 5% of tax payable if tax not remitted; criminal prosecution for willful evasion

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 (Quebec Partnership Return) – Revenu Québec Cliquez
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after fiscal year-end (same as federal)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Quebec-source income; non-resident partners must file Quebec return if they have a permanent establishment in Quebec

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses deductible for Quebec purposes (must align with federal but may differ)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners cannot claim Quebec-specific credits unless eligible
Provide each partner with a Relevé 15 (RL-15) slip; non-resident partners must file Quebec return if taxable

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: $25 per day per partner, up to $2,500 per partner; additional penalty of 5% of tax payable; interest on unpaid amounts

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (statutory dividend withholding tax for non-residents; LP distributions are not dividends, but if treated as dividends under domestic law, rate applies)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, non-resident partner must provide a Certificate of Residence (Form NR116) to the partnership; partnership submits Form NR302 to CRA and Form Re-1016 to Revenu Québec. Treaty rates may reduce withholding to 0% for interest and 10% for royalties under Canada-US treaty; for dividends, treaty rate is 15% (5% for substantial shareholding).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 25% for royalties and interest; treaty rates may reduce to 0% for interest and 10% for royalties under Canada-US treaty; other treaties vary.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 for gross related-party transactions in goods; CAD 500,000 for services; CAD 250,000 for other transactions
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) but applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and requires substantial business purpose for treaty benefits. Partnerships must demonstrate real commercial activity, adequate staff, and premises in Canada to avoid treaty shopping challenges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting income, inflating expenses, or falsifying records related to import transactions (e.g., underreporting customs value, misclassifying goods)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to 200% of tax evaded; imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties under Income Tax Act and Excise Tax Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners may be personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they fail to withhold or remit; travel bans and asset seizure possible

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a pass-through entity without real economic substance (e.g., no physical office, no employees, no business activity in Canada) to avoid tax or obtain treaty benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits; reassessment of income; penalties up to 50% of tax avoided; potential criminal charges for fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties; court orders for restitution; travel bans if non-compliance persists

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML compliance program, report suspicious transactions, or maintain records for large cash payments (over CAD 10,000) in import/export activities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 2 million for corporations; criminal fines up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for individuals
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers can be personally fined and imprisoned if they knowingly fail to comply; civil liability for damages; travel bans and asset freezes
